question: What do all the reviews on this condition say, side by side?

ioannidis2009.cite: Ioannidis (2009). Integration of evidence from multiple meta-analyses: a primer on umbrella reviews, treatment networks and multiple treatments meta-analyses. CMAJ 181(8): 488–493.
ioannidis2009.checked: every quote read word for word on the PMC article page (PMC2761440) in Chrome on 20 Nov 2026; volume and pages as printed there; places are given as the article's section headings; in-text reference numbers are left out of the quotes

steps.title: Frame it wide
steps.text: Name the condition and, up front, every treatment and outcome the umbrella will cover.

quotes.text: Umbrella reviews (Figure 1) are systematic reviews that consider many treatment comparisons for the management of the same disease or condition.
Umbrella reviews may be better to perform prospectively, defining upfront the range of interventions and outcomes that are to be addressed.

steps.title: Gather the reviews
steps.text: Find the systematic reviews and meta-analyses for each comparison, and keep those of good enough quality.

quotes.text: Umbrella reviews are clusters that encompass many reviews.

steps.title: Line them up
steps.text: Treat each comparison separately, and set benefits and harms side by side across all of them.

quotes.text: Each comparison is considered separately, and meta-analyses are performed as deemed appropriate.
Compared with a systematic review or meta-analysis limited to 1 treatment comparison or even 1 outcome, an umbrella review can provide a wider picture on many treatments.

steps.title: Mind the seams
steps.text: The reviews used different criteria and were updated at different times, and some options were never reviewed. Say so.

quotes.text: Patching together pre-existing reviews is limited by different eligibility criteria, evaluation methods and thoroughness of updating information across the merged reviews.
Finally, qualitative juxtaposition of data from separate meta-analyses is subjective and suboptimal.

limits: Grading the credibility of each meta-analysis (as in Theodoratou et al. 2014, the card's example) is not covered: that paper was not read.
Ioannidis (2009) defines umbrella reviews over treatments for one condition; later umbrella reviews also cover risk factors, as the vitamin D example does.
The step texts in our own words are summaries of the quotes beside them; the quotes are the authority.
